title: Invasive, Randomized, Crossover, Sham-controlled Study on the Interaction Between CMD and HFpEF
official: Coronary Microvascular Function Assessment in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the prevalence of coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction, define new endotypes according to hemodynamic changes, invasively assess the influence of preload modulation in microvascular resistance, coronary sinus modulation on left ventricular hemodynamics (contractility, relaxation and stiffness), detect key factors in multiomics analysis that influence myocardial ischemia and endothelial function, in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction (HpEF).
conditions: HFpEF - Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF ≥50%), with dyspnoea of at least NYHA class II and/or angina pectoris of at least CCS class I
* Indication for left/right heart catheterisation, including microvascular function testing
* Willingness to participate and ability to understand, read and sign the informed consent;
* Age\>18 years

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age \<18 years;
* Acute coronary syndrome;
* Hemodynamic collapse/decompensation at presentation;
* Severe valvular cardiomyopathy or other cardiomyopathies (hypertrophic, amyloidosis, M. Fabry)
* Reduced ejection fraction, EF\<50%
* Reduced eGFR\<30 mL/min/1.73 m²
* Reduced life expectancy (\<1 year)
* Previous CABG with patent grafts to the left anterior descending coronary
* Epicardial coronary disease (FFR \<0.80 with evidence of a focal stenosis) in the left anterior descending territory
* Pregnancy
* Inability to provide informed consent
